deps.summary: The dependency set is split roughly into three groups. The Kotlin/coroutines/Koin-core foundation is already KMP-ready and can move directly to commonMain. A mid-tier of Jetpack libraries (Room 2.8, DataStore 1.2, Lifecycle ViewModel 2.10, navigation-compose via JetBrains fork, Compose UI/Material3 via JetBrains CMP artifacts) all have KMP equivalents that require only groupId swaps or minor configuration changes. The legacy View layer — appcompat, MDC-Material, Fragment, RecyclerView, ViewPager2, ConstraintLayout-View, asynclayoutinflater, Glide, colorpickerview — represents about one-third of dependencies and will disappear entirely once the in-flight Compose migration completes; no KMP porting effort is needed for these. The most significant platform-specific concerns that require expect/actual interfaces are: image loading (Coil 2 must upgrade to Coil 3 CMP), EXIF orientation reading (exifinterface), Palette color extraction, image compression (id.zelory compressor), Android permissions (accompanist-permissions), and the cmonet dynamic-color module. The WaterMarkImageView custom View embedded via AndroidView in EditorScreen is the deepest blocking item for iOS/Desktop targets and will need to be rewritten as a pure Compose Canvas composable.

graphicsCore.summary: EasyWatermark's rendering engine is a compact (~500 LOC) android.graphics pipeline centered on one trick: render the watermark (text or icon) once into a small offscreen ARGB_8888 Bitmap "cell", wrap it in a BitmapShader, and fill a rect with that shader — TileMode.REPEAT tiles it across the whole photo, TileMode.CLAMP (called "decal"/single in the UI) draws one draggable instance. The cell builders (`WaterMarkImageView.buildTextBitmapShader` / `buildIconBitmapShader`, app/src/main/java/me/rosuh/easywatermark/ui/widget/WaterMarkImageView.kt:600-775) are static and SHARED by preview and export, but the final composition is DUPLICATED: preview in `WaterMarkImageView.onDraw` (view canvas over a subsampled bitmap), export in `MainViewModel.generateImage` (app/src/main/java/me/rosuh/easywatermark/ui/MainViewModel.kt:268-458, Canvas over a full-res mutable bitmap, then Bitmap.compress JPEG/PNG to MediaStore). Export fidelity is coupled to the preview View's measured size via ViewInfo (scale = 1/imageMatrix.MSCALE_X), and the engine still lives inside an AndroidView in EditorScreen (EditorScreen.kt:674). Every drawing primitive used has a 1:1 or near-1:1 equivalent in androidx.compose.ui.graphics (ImageBitmap+Canvas, ImageShader+TileMode.Repeated, TextMeasurer/drawText, Paint, DrawScope transforms); only decode (BitmapFactory/inSampleSize/EXIF) and encode (Bitmap.compress) genuinely need expect/actual. A single commonMain rewrite is feasible and would also eliminate the preview/export duplication and the ViewInfo coupling. Highest-risk areas: text shaping/font parity on iOS/Desktop (Skia paragraph vs StaticLayout, emoji 👋 in the default watermark, zh/ja/fa locales), full-res memory on iOS (no catchable OOM, no subsampled decode in Skiko), color-space drift (P3 iPhone photos vs forced sRGB), and JPEG quality/EXIF-stripping semantics.

graphicsCore.recommendation:
Option (a): rewrite the engine ONCE in commonMain on androidx.compose.ui.graphics, with a single offscreen-ImageBitmap renderer shared by preview AND export, and only decode/encode/storage behind expect/actual. Do NOT keep the engine per-platform (option b): the portable core is only ~400-500 lines (two cell builders + one composition rule + one scale rule, already factored as static functions in WaterMarkImageView's companion), every drawing primitive has a direct common equivalent (ImageBitmap(w,h)+Canvas, DrawScope withTransform/rotate/translate, ImageShader+TileMode.Repeated/Clamp via ShaderBrush, TextMeasurer.measure+drawText, Paint alpha/style), and an expect/actual engine would force maintaining android.graphics and a Skia twin while still having to prove pixel parity between a common preview and per-platform exports — the worst of both worlds. The rewrite also retires the two real design debts found in the code: (1) the duplicated composition logic (WaterMarkImageView.onDraw vs MainViewModel.generateImage lines 371-391) and (2) the ViewInfo coupling, where export scale = 1/imageMatrix.MSCALE_X of the on-screen view (MainViewModel.kt:301-324) so export output literally depends on the preview widget's measured size (and export is blocked until the view reports ViewInfo, ComposeMainActivity.kt:254-255) — on Desktop with resizable windows this would be a correctness bug, so the new engine must size watermarks in image-space units (e.g. textSize as a fraction of image width), which is a deliberate behavior change needing a config migration for persisted textSize.

Target shape: commonMain `WatermarkRenderer` with (i) `buildCell(config, density-free TextMeasurer or icon ImageBitmap, scale): ImageBitmap` — text via TextMeasurer.measure (which natively gives max line width and line metrics, replacing the manual measureText loop and the StaticLayout vertical-centering hack), icon via drawImage with explicit FilterQuality; (ii) `composite(drawScope, photoSize, cell, tileMode, offset)` — one draw lambda using ShaderBrush(ImageShader(cell, Repeated)) for tile mode and drawImage at fractional offset for single mode, invoked by BOTH the Compose preview Canvas and an offscreen `ImageBitmap(w,h)+Canvas+CanvasDrawScope` export rasterizer; (iii) expect/actual: `decodeImage(handle, targetSize)` (subsampled; BitmapFactory / CGImageSourceCreateThumbnailAtIndex or Skia+downscale / Skia), `encodeImage(bitmap, format, quality)` (Bitmap.compress / Skia encodeToData), `readOrientation(handle)`, `savePhoto(bytes)` (MediaStore / PHPhotoLibrary / file dialog). Platform-neutral models first: strip Shader.TileMode, android.net.Uri, Bitmap.CompressFormat, Matrix/ScaleType out of WaterMark/ImageInfo/ViewInfo/UserPreferences (they currently leak android types into the data layer and into DataStore ordinals — keep explicit ordinal-compatible mappers).

WHEN: now, as the NEXT step of the in-flight View->Compose migration — before porting more option panels and before any KMP project restructuring. WaterMarkImageView is the last load-bearing legacy View inside EditorScreen (AndroidView at EditorScreen.kt:674), and replacing it is simultaneously the completion of the Compose migration and the creation of the CMP engine; doing panels first would build more UI on top of the ViewInfo/AndroidView contract that must die. Concretely: (1) platform-neutral model layer + mappers; (2) write the renderer inside :app using ONLY androidx.compose.ui.graphics/ui.text imports (it compiles unchanged on Android today — 'commonMain-ready' without yet having a shared module), with golden-image tests asserting new-export == old-export on a corpus (multiline text, 315°, emoji, CJK, both tile modes, icon mode, JPEG+PNG); (3) swap EditorScreen's AndroidView for a Compose Canvas preview driven by the renderer (gestures via pointerInput, fade/snap-back via Animatable), keeping ALL existing pixel conventions (tile origin at photo top-left, gap = size*(g/100+1), diagonal cell for icons, rotation-AABB formula); (4) point MainViewModel.generateImage at the renderer + Android encode actuals and delete WaterMarkImageView/WaterMarkShader/ViewInfo; (5) when the repo restructures to CMP, lift the renderer file into shared commonMain verbatim and implement the iOS/Desktop actuals. Estimated effort: the renderer itself is days, not weeks; the long poles are decode/encode actuals on iOS, photo-library storage, and parity testing.
risks: Text shaping/font parity: Android CMP keeps platform text, but iOS/Desktop render through Skia Paragraph with different default fonts (no Roboto on iOS), different fallback chains, hinting and line metrics. The DEFAULT watermark text begins with an emoji ("👋 DO NOT REDISTRIBUTE", data/model/WaterMark.kt:34) and the app ships zh/ja/fa locales — emoji color-font fallback, CJK fallback, and RTL/Farsi shaping must be verified per target. The vertical-centering formula uses StaticLayout first-line metrics ((finalHeight - lineBottom(0) - lineTop(0))/2, WaterMarkImageView.kt:757) and Paint.Align.CENTER horizontal trickery — re-derive from TextLayoutResult metrics, never copy. Bundle one font via compose-resources for determinism.

Pixel parity preview<->export and old<->new: tile pitch depends on measured text width, so a few-px difference between Paint.measureText and TextMeasurer changes the repeat pattern across the whole image; rotation-AABB (w*cos+h*sin), gap percentage, icon diagonal cell, and CLAMP fractional-offset conventions must be reproduced exactly or golden tests will catch drift. Note duplicated-line measurement uses text.indexOf(line) (WaterMarkImageView.kt:698) — a latent bug; decide to preserve or fix, document either way.

Color management: BitmapFactory converts to sRGB by default, while Skia decode on iOS/Desktop can preserve wide-gamut (Display-P3 is standard for iPhone photos) — exported colors and the watermark color may shift between platforms. Pin a policy: decode to sRGB N32 everywhere (and check ImageBitmapConfig/ColorSpace when constructing offscreen bitmaps).

EXIF orientation and metadata: current behavior bakes orientation into pixels at decode (BitmapUtils.kt:55-66) and STRIPS all other metadata (GPS/date/camera) on export — no ExifInterface write exists. Skia ignores EXIF orientation entirely, so a naive Skiko decode produces sideways images on iOS/Desktop unless orientation is applied manually (Coil 3 handles it). interChangeSize (BitmapUtils.kt:214-220) swaps width/height for 90°/180° instead of 90°/270° — a latent bug; don't port it blindly. Decide explicitly whether metadata stripping is a privacy FEATURE (likely, for this app) and document it, because iOS photo-library save APIs can silently re-attach metadata.

iOS memory limits: export decodes the photo FULL-RES then makes an ARGB_8888 .copy (MainViewModel.kt:274-283) — a 48MP photo means ~200MB+ in two (sometimes three, with EXIF rotation) simultaneous buffers. Android catches OutOfMemoryError (TYPE_ERROR_SAVE_OOM); Kotlin/Native has NO catchable OOM and iOS jetsam kills the process well before the nominal limit. The CMP engine must decode straight into the mutable target (drop the copy), cap export resolution or tile the composition, and use CGImageSourceCreateThumbnailAtIndex-style bounded decode — also note Skiko has no inSampleSize equivalent, so a naive port decodes full-res even for PREVIEW (today's preview is always subsampled, inSampleSize >= 2 by construction, BitmapUtils.kt:232).

JPEG/PNG encoding semantics: Bitmap.compress(JPEG, 80) on Android (libjpeg-turbo + Android color converter) vs Skia EncodedImageFormat.JPEG at the same quality number yields different file sizes and artifact patterns; PNG ignores quality (current UI exposes a 20-100 level even for PNG, UserConfigRepository.kt:40-42). JPEG has no alpha: Android composites transparent pixels to black on compress — verify Skia's behavior so semi-transparent watermark edges don't differ. Keep the 'level snapped to multiples of 20, min 20' coercion or migrate it consciously.

TileMode persistence: DataStore stores android Shader.TileMode.ordinal (WaterMarkRepository.kt:152) and deserializes via toTileMode() (IntExtension.kt:47) including MIRROR/DECAL values the UI can't set. Compose TileMode enumerates Clamp/Repeated/Mirror/Decal in the same order today, but relying on cross-enum ordinal equality is fragile — introduce an app-owned enum with explicit ordinal-compatible mapping before models go common; also note TileMode.Decal needs API 31 on Android (current code gates the same way) but works everywhere on Skia — a capability asymmetry to gate in common code.

ViewInfo/behavior change: moving from view-size-derived export scale (1/MSCALE_X) to image-space watermark sizing changes WHAT existing persisted configs/templates mean (textSize 14f is currently view-px at preview scale, and preview is density-dependent since textSize is raw px, PainKtx.kt:23). Requires a one-time config migration and product sign-off; skipping this makes Desktop exports window-size-dependent — a real bug, not just a quirk.

Icon scaling quality: createScaledBitmap(filter=false) is nearest-neighbor (WaterMarkImageView.kt:636-640) — crunchy by design today; Skia/Compose default sampling is bilinear, so icon watermarks will look smoother/different unless FilterQuality.None is pinned (or the change is accepted and screenshot baselines updated).

Threading/lifecycle: preview serializes cell building on a single-thread executor specifically to make Bitmap.recycle safe (WaterMarkImageView.kt:102-108) while export uses Dispatchers.IO on the same functions; ImageBitmap has no recycle(), removing that hazard but adding GC-pressure risk on iOS/K-N for large pixel buffers — keep the serialization for cancellation semantics (generateBitmapJob?.cancel()) and add explicit buffer reuse if profiling demands it.

Android-only dependency cliffs adjacent to the engine: androidx.palette (background color), id.zelory.compressor (compressImg pre-shrink path), Glide 5 (legacy thumbnails) and MediaStore/FileProvider storage all need replace-or-drop decisions; iOS adds a brand-new PHPhotoLibrary permission/UX flow for saving that has no Android analogue in the current code.

Dead/duplicated code traps for the porter: BitmapUtils.generateMatrix (BitmapUtils.kt:327-405, a copy of ImageView's matrix logic) has zero call sites, as do the inBitmap pooling helpers (addInBitmapOptions/getAvailableMemory) — don't waste effort porting them; pinch-to-scale in WaterMarkImageView.onTouchEvent is commented out (lines 501-504) but onScaleEnd plumbing survives into EditorScreen — decide whether to resurrect it in the Compose gesture rewrite.

storageIo.summary: The EasyWatermark app (branch feat/migrate_to_compose) has eight distinct IO flows that must each be re-architected for Compose Multiplatform (Android + iOS + Desktop). All flows currently use Android-only APIs: android.net.Uri, ContentResolver, MediaStore, BitmapFactory, ExifInterface, FileProvider, accompanist-permissions, and Glide/Coil with Android contexts. The core decode/render pipeline (BitmapUtils.kt, WaterMarkImageView.kt) is the deepest Android coupling because it uses ContentResolver.openInputStream, BitmapFactory.decodeStream, and androidx.exifinterface; it must be hidden behind an expect/actual PlatformImageDecoder. The save/export pipeline (MainViewModel.generateImage) uses both the API>=29 MediaStore IS_PENDING insert pattern and a pre-Q Environment.getExternalStoragePublicDirectory path with MediaScannerConnection; for CMP the pre-Q path can be dropped (raise minSdk to 29) and the Q+ path replaced with expect/actual PlatformImageSaver. The gallery-listing flow (MainViewModel.queryInternal) queries MediaStore.Images.Media directly with a 9-column projection; this must become an expect GalleryRepository backed by PHFetchRequest on iOS and directory enumeration on Desktop. The image-picking flow is already the most modern (Photo Picker API via PickMultipleVisualMedia) and maps cleanly to PHPickerViewController on iOS and FileKit on Desktop. EXIF is read-only and used only for rotation correction; the watermarked export via Bitmap.compress intentionally strips all EXIF metadata (data-loss risk). The accompanist-permissions dependency is Android-only and must be replaced with platform-specific permission controllers. The share-in flow (ACTION_SEND on MainActivity) is entirely Android-specific and requires a platform-extension entry point; it is not yet wired into the Compose navigation graph. The share-out flow (ACTION_SEND/ACTION_SEND_MULTIPLE in SaveImageBSDialogFragment) is also Android-only; the SaveExportSheet onShareClick callback is currently empty and needs to route through a PlatformShareSheet expect/actual. Two libraries are Android-only and must be replaced: id.zelory:compressor (used for optional source pre-compression) and accompanist-permissions. Glide is used only in legacy View-based adapters that will be removed during the Compose migration; Coil (already used in Compose screens) has a multiplatform variant (coil3) that supports Android, iOS, and Desktop and is the recommended display-layer image library for CMP.
risks: EXIF strip on export: Bitmap.compress and iOS/Desktop equivalents all discard EXIF metadata (GPS, camera model, copyright). The watermarked output loses all original metadata. If users expect EXIF preservation (e.g., copyright watermark that should also be embedded in EXIF) this is a silent data-loss behavior that must be explicitly decided before CMP migration.

Pre-Q save path still in codebase: MainViewModel.generateImage has an else branch that uses Environment.getExternalStoragePublicDirectory and WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE permission for API<29. If CMP sets minSdk<29 for the Android target this path must be kept and tested; if minSdk is raised to 29 it can be deleted but the manifest WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE declaration (currently with tools:ignore=ScopedStorage and no maxSdkVersion) will cause a lint warning and potential Play Store policy concern.

MediaStore.Images.Media.DATA column read in gallery listing (MainViewModel.queryInternal line 775): this deprecated column is read and used as a non-null check to skip rows. On Android 11+ (scoped storage) DATA may be null or empty for media not owned by the app. The null-check guard exists but the column is still in the projection, which is unnecessary and may return empty strings that silently drop valid images.

Uri persistence across process death: ImageInfo stores android.net.Uri values. These content:// Uris from Photo Picker are temporary and do not survive process death without takePersistableUriPermission(). If the app is killed and restored from SavedState, the selected image Uris may be invalid. This risk is unchanged by CMP but should be addressed during migration by copying images to the app cache on selection.

Compressor library (id.zelory:compressor 3.0.1) uses File-based API: compressImg() copies the content Uri to a temp File via contentResolver.openInputStream then passes it to Compressor.compress(activity, tmpFile). On Android 10+ this works but the file lands in the app's internal cache. This library is Android-only and its replacement on iOS/Desktop requires native equivalents. The Compressor flow is triggered by OOM errors during save (CompressImageDialogFragment); without a cross-platform replacement OOM handling would silently fail on iOS/Desktop.

ACTION_SEND share-in only handles single image (intent.data), ignoring clipData for multi-image share: the manifest only registers ACTION_SEND, not ACTION_SEND_MULTIPLE. Apps sharing multiple images will only deliver the first image or fail silently. This is an existing Android-only gap unrelated to CMP but should be fixed before migration.

WaterMarkImageView.kt as AndroidView in EditorScreen: the watermark preview is implemented as a custom AppCompatImageView embedded via AndroidView. It uses Canvas, BitmapShader, and TextPaint which have identical APIs on Android SDK and Compose Canvas. However the full rewrite to a Compose Canvas-based implementation is required for iOS/Desktop targets since AndroidView does not exist outside Android. The shader-based watermark tiling logic (buildTextBitmapShader, buildIconBitmapShader) can be ported to androidx.compose.ui.graphics.Canvas but the paint/shader APIs differ on iOS (Skia-backed in CMP but with some limitations on Metal).

Glide as legacy display dependency: Glide 5 (AppGlideModule, GlideBuilder.setDefaultRequestOptions with RGB_565) is used in SaveImageListAdapter, PhotoListPreviewAdapter, and ImageViewKtx. These are View-based components that will be removed during Compose migration, but until they are removed Glide and Coil coexist, doubling the image loading overhead. When the legacy adapters are removed, the GlideModule and glide/glide-compiler dependencies can be deleted.

DataStore (androidx.datastore:datastore-preferences) is used for UserPreferences (outputFormat, compressLevel): it is Android-only unless replaced with a multiplatform DataStore or an alternative like multiplatform-settings (russhwolf). The CMP migration must decide on a settings persistence library before migrating UserConfigRepository.

ViewInfo couples to android.widget.ImageView: ViewInfo.from(imageView: ImageView) extracts width/height/padding/scaleType/imageMatrix from a live Android View. This is used to pass rendering context from the legacy WaterMarkImageView to the export pipeline in MainViewModel.generateImage. When WaterMarkImageView is replaced with a Compose Canvas, ViewInfo must be populated from LayoutCoordinates or a Compose-side measurement callback instead.

stateIssues: Dual state exposure for watermark config: waterMark is a LiveData<WaterMark> (line 87) AND waterMarkFlow is a StateFlow<WaterMark> (lines 89-93) derived from the same source. Both are live simultaneously and consumers may observe either, creating two subscription chains for the same data. waterMark (LiveData) must be deleted; all collectors must migrate to waterMarkFlow before the ViewModel can be commonized.

saveResult is MutableLiveData<Result<*>> (line 83) with no StateFlow counterpart. saveImage() writes to saveResult.value on the main thread (lines 223-231) while generateList() uses saveProcess.postValue() from a background coroutine (lines 247, 255, 259, 264). MutableLiveData has no KMP equivalent. Must be replaced with MutableStateFlow<SaveState> sealed class before moving to commonMain.
compressedResult is MutableLiveData<Result<*>> (line 85) — same issue as saveResult. compressImg() posts to it from Dispatchers.IO (lines 643, 663, 673). Must become a StateFlow.

saveProcess is MutableLiveData<ImageInfo?> (line 116) used both with .value = (line 247, from main-thread launch block) and .postValue() (lines 255, 259, 264 from withContext(Dispatchers.Default)). Mixed .value/.postValue access pattern creates a thread-safety risk and must be unified as a MutableStateFlow<ImageInfo?> before migration.

colorPalette is MutableLiveData<Palette> (line 134) where Palette is android.palette.graphics.Palette — an Android-only type. This LiveData both holds an Android type and uses the LiveData API. Must be decoupled: Palette extraction moves to androidMain, only the extracted color Int travels through a commonMain StateFlow<Int?>.

imageList is LiveData<Pair<List<ImageInfo>, Boolean>> (line 105) derived via waterMarkRepo.imageInfoMapFlow.asLiveData().map { ... }. It bundles autoScroll (a mutable var on the ViewModel, line 103) into the LiveData value. This means autoScroll state is not observable independently and is mutated without going through a flow operator. Must become a data class field in a single StateFlow<EditorUiState> or be tracked as a separate MutableStateFlow<Boolean>.

galleryPickedImageList is MutableLiveData<List<Image>> (line 108) that is posted from queryInternal() (line 799) and also mirrored into _launchScreenUiStateFlow (lines 801-806). The same gallery list is thus maintained in two parallel state holders, risking divergence. Should be collapsed — the StateFlow is the authoritative source and the LiveData removed.

selectedImage is LiveData<ImageInfo> (line 110) backed by waterMarkRepo.selectedImage StateFlow via .asLiveData(). The ViewModel also exposes selectedImageFlow (line 112-113) as the raw StateFlow. Consumers must be unified on the StateFlow; the LiveData bridge must be removed.

saveImageUri is a private MutableLiveData<List<ImageInfo>> (line 114) that is set in saveImage() (line 230) but never observed externally. It is vestigial state that should be removed or folded into the save StateFlow.

The init block launches two coroutines (lines 163-181) that collect waterMarkFlow and selectedImageFlow and re-emit into _launchScreenUiStateFlow using manual withContext(Dispatchers.Main) switches. This is a fragile pattern — it does not use combine() and can emit stale intermediate states if both flows emit near-simultaneously. Should be replaced with a single combine(waterMarkFlow, selectedImageFlow) { wm, img -> ... }.stateIn(...) assignment.

process(action) dispatches Action.WaterMarkChange to onWaterMarkChanged which casts action.any to the expected type (e.g., any as Uri, any as Shader.TileMode — lines 1097, 1114). This untyped dispatch means type errors only surface at runtime. Must be replaced with strongly-typed Action subclasses carrying typed payloads before ViewModel commonization.

outputFormat and compressLevel are computed properties (lines 128-132) that read _userPreferences.value directly — a synchronous StateFlow value access. This is safe on Android but in commonMain the StateFlow.value read is allowed; however both properties appear on the ViewModel class itself while saveOutput() (line 585) launches a coroutine to update them. The mismatch between eager property reads and async updates can cause a race if saveOutput is called immediately after a format change. Should be resolved by consolidating into userPreferences StateFlow only.

- data/model/ImageInfo.kt — swap android.net.Uri field for expect/actual ImageUri
- data/model/UserPreferences.kt — replace Bitmap.CompressFormat with shared ImageFormat sealed class
- data/repo/UserConfigRepository.kt — same ImageFormat swap + DataStore KMP artifact
- data/model/entity/Template.kt — remove Parcelable, replace java.util.Date with kotlinx.datetime.Instant, Room 2.7+ annotations are KMP-safe
- data/db/AppDatabase + TemplateDao + DateConverter — Room 2.7 KMP coordinates; keep databaseBuilder in androidMain expect/actual
- data/repo/WaterMarkRepository.kt — replace Uri/Color/Shader/ArrayMap/MyApp.getString; DataStore KMP artifact; then move to commonMain
- data/model/WaterMark.kt — replace Uri+Shader.TileMode+Color.parseColor; introduce shared TileMode enum
- data/model/TextPaintStyle.kt / TextTypeface.kt — remove View-system applyStyle methods; extract int constants to commonMain
- data/model/FuncTitleModel.kt — move FuncType sealed hierarchy to commonMain; keep resource-ID-carrying class in androidMain
- data/repo/MemorySettingRepo.kt — replace Palette with a plain Int; inject CoroutineScope
- ui/Image.kt — replace android.net.Uri
- di/ (Koin modules) — koin-core to commonMain; Room builder / DataStore preferencesDataStore stays androidMain

Needs major redesign before KMP (keep in androidMain for now):
- ui/MainViewModel.kt — heavy: LiveData/MutableLiveData pervasive; ContentResolver/MediaStore image querying; Activity passed into compressImg/extraCrashInfo; WaterMarkImageView static method calls from generateImage; inject(Context) via KoinJavaComponent; Bitmap.CompressFormat/Canvas/Matrix/Paint/Shader/TextPaint all used for rendering logic. The ViewModel itself must be split: a commonMain ViewModel (lifecycle-viewmodel KMP artifact) holding pure state, and an androidMain delegate or use-case for MediaStore access, Bitmap rendering, and file I/O.
- utils/bitmap/BitmapUtils.kt — BitmapFactory + ExifInterface + ContentResolver; keep androidMain; extract matrix math to commonMain
- utils/bitmap/BitmapCache.kt — android.util.LruCache + Bitmap; keep androidMain
- data/model/ViewInfo.kt — android.graphics.Matrix + android.widget.ImageView.ScaleType; will be eliminated when WaterMarkImageView is replaced by Compose Canvas drawing
- utils/ktx/ContextExtension.kt / ActivityKtx.kt / IntExtension.kt / PainKtx.kt / PaletteKtx.kt / ViewExtension.kt / ImageViewKtx.kt — all Android View/Context specific; keep androidMain
- ui/base/* — legacy Fragment/Activity base classes; retire during Compose migration, do not port
- MyApp.kt — Application subclass; keep androidMain; extract applicationScope to shared init

The single biggest blocker is MainViewModel, which mixes 12 LiveData fields with StateFlow fields, embeds MediaStore/ContentResolver/Bitmap rendering logic directly in suspend functions, and passes Activity to two methods. The in-flight state migration on branch feat/migrate_to_compose has already introduced waterMarkFlow and _launchScreenUiStateFlow as StateFlows, which is the right direction, but the parallel LiveData fields (saveResult, compressedResult, saveProcess, imageList, galleryPickedImageList, selectedImage, colorPalette) must all be converted and the rendering/I/O logic extracted to androidMain use-cases before the ViewModel core can be moved to commonMain.

cmonet.purpose: cmonet is a thin Android-only wrapper around Material Components' DynamicColors API that gates wallpaper-driven Monet theming. It does NOT contain any color math or scheme generation of its own. Its sole responsibility is: (1) deciding whether dynamic color is available on the current device by cross-referencing `DynamicColors.isDynamicColorAvailable()` with a hardcoded allowlist of OEM manufacturer/brand strings (Build.MANUFACTURER, Build.BRAND), and (2) persisting a user-controlled override flag ("force enable" / "force disable") in SharedPreferences so the user can bypass that allowlist. When available, it calls `DynamicColors.applyToActivitiesIfAvailable(application)` at app startup to inject wallpaper-extracted color tokens into every Activity's theme.
cmonet.cmpStrategy: Replace / Android-actualize via expect/actual. cmonet is entirely Android-bound (android.app.Application, android.os.Build, android.content.SharedPreferences, com.google.android.material.color.DynamicColors). There is no color math to commonize. On the CMP path the concept becomes a platform-capability query: on Android (androidMain) preserve the current logic (DynamicColors + OEM allowlist + SharedPreferences toggle); on iOS/Desktop provide an expect/actual that simply returns false (dynamic wallpaper color is not available). The toggle persistence should migrate to DataStore Preferences (already used in the app) behind an expect/actual or a shared repository. The Compose theme in Theme.kt already has the right shape — AppTheme has a `dynamicColor: Boolean` parameter, and on Android it calls `dynamicDarkColorScheme(context)` / `dynamicLightColorScheme(context)` directly from material3, bypassing cmonet entirely. The legacy View path (ContextExtension.kt) calls `CMonet.isDynamicColorAvailable()` on every color attribute accessor, but this path is being replaced by Compose and will not survive the CMP migration. There is no need to port the cmonet module as a CMP library; instead, a small androidMain expect/actual for `isDynamicColorAvailable(): Boolean` and the toggle storage is sufficient.
cmonet.summary: cmonet is a thin Android-only gate-keeper module (5 Kotlin files) that wraps `com.google.android.material.color.DynamicColors` to decide whether wallpaper-extracted Monet colors should be applied, using an OEM allowlist against `Build.MANUFACTURER`/`Build.BRAND` plus a SharedPreferences-backed user override. It performs no color science itself. The legacy View layer in `utils/ktx/ContextExtension.kt` calls `CMonet.isDynamicColorAvailable()` on every Material color attribute accessor; however the Compose theme in `ui/Theme.kt` bypasses cmonet entirely and calls `dynamicDarkColorScheme`/`dynamicLightColorScheme` directly from material3, with the `dynamicColor` parameter currently hard-coded to `false` at the `AppTheme` call site in `ComposeMainActivity`. For CMP the module should be replaced: the dynamic-color query becomes an androidMain `actual` that replicates the OEM allowlist, the toggle persistence moves to DataStore (already in the project), iOS and Desktop receive a trivially-returning `false` actual, and the brand-color fallback palettes already defined as `LightColorScheme`/`DarkColorScheme` in `Theme.kt` serve as the static fallback for non-Android targets. Verdict: do not port cmonet to commonMain; replace it with a thin expect/actual capability wrapper and remove the module from the Compose-path dependency graph entirely.
cmonet.androidCoupling: Heavy, exclusively Android-bound. Concrete dependencies: android.app.Application (CMonet.init parameter, MonetManufacturer constructor), android.os.Build.MANUFACTURER and Build.BRAND (OEM allowlist check in MonetManufacturer.isDynamicColorAvailable), android.content.Context and android.content.SharedPreferences / Context.MODE_PRIVATE (SimpleSp persistence), com.google.android.material.color.DynamicColors.isDynamicColorAvailable() and DynamicColors.applyToActivitiesIfAvailable() (the actual wallpaper-color source). The build.gradle.kts declares id(libs.plugins.android.library), core-ktx, appcompat, and material as dependencies — all Android-only artifacts. There is no Kotlin-only or KMP-compatible code in the module.

kmpStructure.summary: Research on the official JetBrains-recommended path to migrate an existing Android Jetpack Compose app (like EasyWatermark, single :app module, Kotlin 2.3.20, AGP 8.13.2) to Kotlin Multiplatform + Compose Multiplatform targeting Android, iOS, and Desktop. CMP 1.11.0 (May 2026) is the current release. iOS has been stable since CMP 1.8.0 (May 2025). All six research questions are answered below with source citations.

findings.topic: Recommended Gradle project layout: single composeApp module vs shared+thin platform modules
findings.guidance: JetBrains recommends starting with a SINGLE shared module (conventionally named composeApp or shared) that holds all common UI and logic, with thin platform entry-point modules (androidApp, iosApp, desktopApp) that simply depend on it. The compose-multiplatform-ios-android-template and the official 'Create your Compose Multiplatform app' tutorial both use this layout. For an EXISTING single-:app-module Android app, the prescribed path is: (1) keep the existing app module as the Android entry point (or extract a thin androidApp wrapper), (2) create a new composeApp/shared KMP library module where all common code lives. The official 'Migrating a Jetpack Compose app to Kotlin Multiplatform' guide explicitly states that modularization is a prerequisite: the app must be split into entry-point module(s) plus shared code module(s) before KMP is applied. A separated sharedLogic + sharedUI layout is only recommended when some platforms will keep native (Swift) UI, which is not the case for full Compose Multiplatform. AGP 9+ enforces this separation by requiring that the KMP shared module use com.android.kotlin.multiplatform.library (not com.android.application), making a standalone thin androidApp module with com.android.application mandatory if you want to stay on AGP 9+.

findings.topic: Official step sequence for converting an existing Android app to KMP
findings.guidance: The official migrate-from-android.html guide prescribes this ordered sequence: (1) Pre-migration checklist — convert all Java code to Kotlin, audit Android/JVM-only dependencies and find multiplatform alternatives, address modularisation debt, migrate Views to Jetpack Compose if not done already. (2) Migrate to multiplatform-compatible libraries first (e.g., Room multiplatform, DataStore multiplatform, kotlinx-coroutines instead of RxJava). (3) Convert business logic modules to KMP incrementally, starting with modules that have the fewest dependencies (innermost: data, domain), applying the kotlin-multiplatform Gradle plugin IN PLACE on existing modules rather than creating new ones (the Jetcaster sample demonstrates this). (4) Create a new shared UI module (composeApp/sharedUI) and migrate screens one at a time to commonMain. (5) Add platform entry points for iOS/Desktop. Each step must leave the app in a working state. For a SINGLE existing :app module (like EasyWatermark), the guide recommends first splitting into feature/layer modules before applying KMP, since KMP works by converting individual modules. The androidTarget() block goes inside kotlin {} in build.gradle.kts alongside iosArm64(), iosSimulatorArm64(), and optionally jvm() for Desktop. With Kotlin 2.3.0+ and AGP 8.x the form is still kotlin { androidTarget { ... } }, but AGP 9 requires migration to the androidLibrary { } block inside kotlin {} with the com.android.kotlin.multiplatform.library plugin.

findings.topic: iOS integration options: XCFramework, CocoaPods, Swift Package Manager, direct Xcode
findings.guidance: Official docs (multiplatform-ios-integration-overview.html) present four options without deprecating any as of mid-2026: (1) Direct Integration via Xcode build phase script — default when using the KMP IDE plugin, simplest, but cannot use CocoaPods dependencies inside the KMP project. (2) Local Swift Package Manager — for mono-repo setups with Swift packages, no CocoaPods needed. (3) Remote SwiftPM with XCFramework — export XCFramework and publish as Swift package; best for explicitly separated codebases or third-party distribution. (4) CocoaPods integration (local or remote with XCFramework) — use when the KMP project itself needs CocoaPods dependencies. CocoaPods is NOT deprecated in official documentation as of June 2026. The August 2025 roadmap focuses on Swift Export improvements and Swift 6.2/Xcode 26 support but does not announce CocoaPods deprecation. XCFramework is a cross-cutting concern rather than a standalone option — it is the binary format used by both SwiftPM remote and CocoaPods remote distributions. For EasyWatermark (no CocoaPods dependencies currently), Direct Integration or Local SwiftPM are the lowest-friction starting points.

findings.topic: expect/actual vs interface-injection official guidance
findings.guidance: The official expect-actual.html guidance strongly prefers interfaces over expect/actual for most cases: 'As a general rule, rely on standard language constructs wherever possible instead of using expected and actual declarations.' Interfaces are preferred because they allow multiple implementations per platform, are easier to test/mock, and don't constrain design. Expected and actual CLASSES are still in Beta (require -Xexpect-actual-classes compiler flag to suppress the warning). Expect/actual is recommended only for: factory functions returning platform implementations, properties needing platform-specific init, singletons that differ per platform, cases requiring inheritance from a platform class, and enumerations needing platform extensions. For DI-heavy projects (EasyWatermark uses Koin 4.2.1): the official guidance is explicit — 'If you already use the DI framework to manage dependencies in your project, we recommend using the same approach for managing platform dependencies.' This means defining a Kotlin interface in commonMain and providing platform-specific implementations injected via Koin modules in androidMain/iosMain, with expect/actual only used to wire the Koin module itself (expect val platformModule: Module).

findings.topic: CMP platform stability as of mid-2026 and Kotlin version pairing
findings.guidance: Current CMP version is 1.11.0 (released May 2026), corresponding to Jetpack Compose 1.11.2. iOS became stable with CMP 1.8.0 (May 2025) — 'all major APIs are now officially stable' with strong compatibility guarantees; concurrent rendering is now ON by default since 1.11.0. Desktop (JVM) is stable. Web/Wasm is functional (touch/scroll was reworked in 1.11.0) but is not listed as fully stable in the same terms as iOS. The general versioning rule from compose-compatibility-and-versioning.html: 'The latest Compose Multiplatform is always compatible with the latest version of Kotlin — no manual version alignment is needed.' Minimum Kotlin for CMP 1.8.0+ is 2.1.0; recommended for projects targeting iOS or web is 2.2.20+. CMP 1.11.0 with Kotlin 2.3.20 is supported — Kotlin 2.3.20 is listed as required for Kotlin/JS and Kotlin/Wasm targets and is within the documented compatible range. AGP constraint: Kotlin 2.3.20 supports AGP 8.2.2–9.0.0; EasyWatermark's AGP 8.13.2 falls within this range (the upper bound is 9.0.0 for Kotlin 2.3.10+, and 8.13.0 specifically for 2.3.0 but not 2.3.20). No blocking incompatibility between Kotlin 2.3.20, AGP 8.13.2, and CMP 1.11.0 has been identified in official docs. KNOWN ISSUE: A known bug in Compose compiler 2.0.0 causes incorrect stability inference for types in multiplatform projects with non-JVM targets, potentially causing unnecessary recompositions; this is a compile-time correctness issue, not a build blocker.

findings.topic: Compiler/runtime plugin interplay: org.jetbrains.compose + compose-compiler + androidx BOM
findings.guidance: Since Kotlin 2.0.0 / CMP 1.6.10, a breaking change requires ALL Compose (including Jetpack Compose) projects to use the new Compose compiler Gradle plugin: id 'org.jetbrains.kotlin.plugin.compose' with the SAME version as the Kotlin plugin (2.3.20). The old embedded compiler approach no longer works. EasyWatermark's existing androidx BOM setup must add this plugin. In a CMP project, both plugins are required: alias(libs.plugins.composeMultiplatform) (org.jetbrains.compose, version is the CMP version e.g. 1.11.0) and alias(libs.plugins.composeCompiler) (org.jetbrains.kotlin.plugin.compose, version matches Kotlin version). ARTIFACT STRATEGY in commonMain/androidMain: In commonMain, use org.jetbrains.compose.* artifacts (e.g. compose.material3, compose.foundation). Gradle Module Metadata causes these to automatically resolve to their androidx.compose.* equivalents when building for Android, so no manual androidMain override is needed for the UI layer. The androidx.compose BOM should NOT be applied to the shared KMP module's commonMain — it is Android-only. For Android-exclusive APIs in androidMain (e.g. activity-compose, appcompat), you can and should declare them as androidMain dependencies using the standard androidx coordinates. The org.jetbrains.compose.runtime:runtime artifact now serves as an alias for the fully-multiplatform androidx.compose.runtime:runtime. Libraries required only on Android (e.g. Coil 2.7.0 Android engine, Room Android artifacts) go in androidMain dependencies. For the androidApp thin wrapper module, the standard android {} block with androidx BOM continues to work normally.

findings.topic: AGP 9 migration path and androidTarget deprecation relevance for EasyWatermark
findings.guidance: EasyWatermark is on AGP 8.13.2, which is compatible with Kotlin 2.3.20 without the androidTarget deprecation issue (the warning was introduced in 2.3.0 then reverted in 2.3.10). On AGP 8.x with Kotlin 2.3.20, the kotlin { androidTarget { } } block continues to work. However, if the project upgrades to AGP 9.0+ during or after the CMP migration, it MUST migrate to: replace com.android.library plugin with com.android.kotlin.multiplatform.library, replace the android {} block with kotlin.androidLibrary {}, extract a thin androidApp module using com.android.application, and change dependency configuration from debugImplementation to androidRuntimeClasspath for tooling artifacts. KNOWN BUG: YouTrack CMP-9547 reports that Compose Multiplatform resources are NOT packaged into the Android APK when using AGP 9.0.0 with com.android.kotlin.multiplatform.library — monitor this before adopting AGP 9. Legacy APIs will be fully removed in AGP 10 (expected H2 2026), so the AGP 9 migration is non-optional on a 12-18 month horizon.

androidxKmp.summary: As of June 2026, the full androidx-on-KMP support matrix for EasyWatermark's dependencies is as follows. All core Jetpack libraries used in this project (Room, DataStore, Lifecycle/ViewModel, Navigation) have reached stable KMP status targeting Android + iOS + JVM Desktop, but several require coordinate changes (org.jetbrains.androidx.* mirrors), API-level surgery (suspend-only DAO functions, OkioStorage/NSFileManager path setup), and build system changes (per-target KSP declarations). Navigation is at a fork: the current androidx.navigation 2.9.x is in maintenance mode; Nav3 (1.1.2) is stable on Android but its UI artifact is Android-only, making it a near-total rewrite for cross-platform use. Room 3.0 (alpha06) adds WASM/JS and changes the group ID to androidx.room3, but the 2.8.4 stable series is the production-safe KMP path today. The org.jetbrains.androidx.* coordinate system wraps the original androidx.* artifacts: on Android the Gradle plugin routes to the original android artifact, on other platforms it uses JetBrains-built variants — the two do NOT need to coexist manually; using org.jetbrains.androidx.* in commonMain is sufficient and correct.

findings.topic: Room — KMP status and version
findings.guidance: Room 2.7.0+ is the minimum for KMP; 2.8.4 (current stable) supports Android, iOS (arm64, x64, simulatorArm64), JVM Desktop, macOS native, Linux native, watchOS, tvOS. iOS support is stable. Room 3.0.0-alpha06 (June 3 2026) adds JS and WASM targets but changes the group ID to androidx.room3 and is alpha only — do not use in production for this migration. Stick with 2.8.4 for the CMP migration. Minimum SDK was raised to API 23 in 2.8.0.

findings.topic: Room — KMP artifact coordinates
findings.guidance: Coordinates are unchanged: androidx.room:room-runtime:2.8.4, androidx.room:room-compiler:2.8.4 (KSP only). Optional: androidx.room:room-sqlite-wrapper:2.8.4 (new in 2.8.0 for backward compat with SupportSQLite code). SQLite bundled driver: androidx.sqlite:sqlite-bundled:2.6.2. No org.jetbrains mirror needed — Room is published by Google as a native KMP artifact.

findings.topic: Room — KSP per-target configuration
findings.guidance: In build.gradle.kts, KSP must be declared for every native target separately. Required additions: add('kspIosSimulatorArm64', libs.androidx.room.compiler), add('kspIosX64', libs.androidx.room.compiler), add('kspIosArm64', libs.androidx.room.compiler). The androidx.room plugin (id 'androidx.room') must also declare schemaLocation for common output. Source: https://developer.android.com/kotlin/multiplatform/room

findings.topic: Room — expect/actual database builder pattern
findings.guidance: The @Database class and @ConstructedBy(AppDatabaseConstructor::class) annotation live in commonMain. AppDatabaseConstructor is an expect object with @Suppress('KotlinNoActualForExpect') — the Room KSP processor generates the actual. Platform builders go in androidMain (using Room.databaseBuilder(context, ...)) and iosMain (using Room.databaseBuilder(name = documentDirectory() + '/app.db')). BundledSQLiteDriver is recommended in commonMain via .setDriver(BundledSQLiteDriver()) for consistent behavior. All DAO query functions must be suspend (no blocking queries) or return Flow. .withTransaction{} is Android-only; use .useWriterConnection { transactor -> transactor.immediateTransaction { } } in common code. Source: https://developer.android.com/kotlin/multiplatform/room

findings.topic: Room — iOS file path via NSFileManager
findings.guidance: iOS builder in iosMain must resolve the path using NSFileManager.defaultManager.URLForDirectory(NSDocumentDirectory, NSUserDomainMask, ...) and append the DB filename. Accessing the path via Android Context pattern will not compile on iOS. NativeSQLiteDriver (alternative to BundledSQLiteDriver) requires linkerOpts.add('-lsqlite3') in the iOS framework block.

findings.topic: Room 3.0 (alpha) — future migration awareness
findings.guidance: Room 3.0.0-alpha06 (June 3 2026) uses new groupId androidx.room3 with artifacts room3-runtime, room3-compiler, room3-paging, room3-sqlite-wrapper. Breaking changes: package rename androidx.room → androidx.room3, removal of all SupportSQLite APIs (Cursor, SupportSQLiteDatabase), KSP-only (KAPT removed), all DAOs must be suspend/Flow, new withWriteTransaction API. Google recommends first migrating to SQLiteDriver APIs in Room 2.8.x, then upgrading to 3.0 when stable. Room 2.x enters maintenance mode. Source: https://developer.android.com/jetpack/androidx/releases/room3

findings.topic: DataStore Preferences — KMP status
findings.guidance: DataStore 1.1.0+ supports KMP; current stable is 1.2.1. Only Preferences DataStore is KMP-compatible; Proto DataStore core (datastore-core) also has KMP support but Proto DataStore's protobuf serializer is platform-specific. iOS support is stable. Supported platforms: Android, iOS, JVM Desktop, Web (JS/WASM added in 1.3.0 alphas). Source: https://developer.android.com/kotlin/multiplatform/datastore

findings.topic: DataStore — KMP artifact coordinates
findings.guidance: For KMP use the -core artifacts in commonMain: androidx.datastore:datastore-preferences-core:1.2.1. The non-core artifact (datastore-preferences:1.2.1) pulls in Android-specific classes and should stay in androidMain. Coordinates are unchanged — no org.jetbrains mirror needed. Source: https://developer.android.com/jetpack/androidx/releases/datastore

findings.topic: DataStore — iOS file path and storage backend
findings.guidance: On iOS, use OkioStorage with FileSystem.SYSTEM and producePath using NSFileManager.defaultManager.URLForDirectory(NSDocumentDirectory). The default storage since 1.1.5 and 1.2.0 switched from OkioStorage to FileStorage for Android to reduce CorruptionException; iOS still requires OkioStorage. okio is an implicit transitive dependency for iOS. The DataStore instance factory function (createDataStore) is declared in commonMain as expect, with iosMain actual providing the NSDocumentDirectory path. Source: https://developer.android.com/kotlin/multiplatform/datastore

findings.topic: Lifecycle + ViewModel 2.10.0 — KMP status
findings.guidance: lifecycle-common, lifecycle-runtime, lifecycle-runtime-compose, lifecycle-viewmodel, lifecycle-viewmodel-compose, lifecycle-viewmodel-savedstate are all fully KMP-stable at 2.10.0 with iOS/JVM/Android tier-1 support. lifecycle-viewmodel-navigation3 has KMP stubs for CMP. 2.11.0-rc01 is available (June 3 2026) with enhanced scoped ViewModel support. MinSDK raised to API 23. lifecycle-runtime-ktx was merged into lifecycle-runtime in 2.10.0. Source: https://developer.android.com/jetpack/androidx/releases/lifecycle

findings.topic: Lifecycle + ViewModel — KMP artifact coordinates
findings.guidance: Artifacts remain under androidx.lifecycle group and can be placed directly in commonMain.dependencies: androidx.lifecycle:lifecycle-viewmodel:2.10.0, androidx.lifecycle:lifecycle-runtime-compose:2.10.0, androidx.lifecycle:lifecycle-viewmodel-compose:2.10.0, androidx.lifecycle:lifecycle-viewmodel-savedstate:2.10.0. No org.jetbrains mirror needed for these. Source: https://developer.android.com/jetpack/androidx/releases/lifecycle

findings.topic: ViewModel — viewModelScope on iOS
findings.guidance: viewModelScope is NOT available on iOS natively — it is tied to Dispatchers.Main.immediate which does not exist on iOS. On iOS coroutines run through the native Kotlin/Native main dispatcher. Practically, ViewModel.viewModelScope works on iOS as of lifecycle 2.8+ through the common ViewModel implementation, but the underlying dispatcher is the Kotlin/Native main dispatcher rather than the JVM Swing/Main dispatcher. For JVM Desktop, you additionally need kotlinx-coroutines-swing in desktopMain. The Koin koinViewModel() composable works in commonMain for both Android and iOS. Source: https://developer.android.com/kotlin/multiplatform/viewmodel

findings.topic: ViewModel — SwiftUI lifecycle bridging
findings.guidance: If Swift/SwiftUI is used directly (not Compose Multiplatform), the ViewModel must be exported to the binary framework (binaries.framework { export(lifecycle-viewmodel) }) and a custom IosViewModelStoreOwner (@StateObject in SwiftUI) that wraps ViewModelStore must be created to manage ViewModel lifecycle. In a full CMP setup (shared Compose UI on iOS via ComposeUIViewController), this is not needed — koinViewModel() and viewModel() work automatically. This project targets full CMP so SwiftUI bridging is not required. Source: https://developer.android.com/kotlin/multiplatform/viewmodel

findings.topic: Koin 4.x — KMP + CMP integration
findings.guidance: Koin 4.x (current 4.2.1) fully supports KMP. Relevant artifacts: io.insert-koin:koin-core (commonMain), io.insert-koin:koin-compose (CMP composables), io.insert-koin:koin-compose-viewmodel (koinViewModel() in commonMain), io.insert-koin:koin-android (androidMain, includes koin-androidx-compose). Hilt is Android-only and cannot be used in commonMain. Koin is the idiomatic DI replacement for a KMP migration. iOS initialization uses KoinKt.doInitKoin() called from the Swift @main struct, or it can be initialized in the shared Kotlin AppModule. Source: https://insert-koin.io/docs/quickstart/cmp/

findings.topic: Navigation — androidx navigation-compose 2.9.x KMP status
findings.guidance: androidx.navigation is in MAINTENANCE MODE as of 2025 — only critical bug fixes, no new features. Latest stable: 2.9.8 (April 22 2026). The navigation-compose artifact (androidx.navigation:navigation-compose) is Android-only. navigation-common and navigation-runtime have KMP support (Android, iOS, JVM, Web, Linux, macOS), but navigation-compose is NOT multiplatform. For CMP, the coordinate to use is org.jetbrains.androidx.navigation:navigation-compose (JetBrains mirror), latest 2.9.2. The JetBrains Compose Multiplatform Gradle plugin auto-routes Android to the original androidx artifact and other platforms to JetBrains-built platform variants. Source: https://developer.android.com/jetpack/androidx/releases/navigation

findings.topic: Navigation — org.jetbrains.androidx.navigation coordinates
findings.guidance: CMP navigation-compose coordinate: org.jetbrains.androidx.navigation:navigation-compose:2.9.2 in commonMain. The Compose Multiplatform Gradle plugin resolves this to androidx.navigation:navigation-compose on Android and to JetBrains-built iOS/Desktop artifacts on other platforms. Type-safe routes require @Serializable on route classes (kotlinx.serialization). On non-JVM platforms (iOS, Web), reflection-based serialization is unavailable so all route classes must use explicit @Serializable annotations — this already applies to the project's existing type-safe navigation setup. Source: https://kotlinlang.org/docs/multiplatform/compose-navigation-routing.html

findings.topic: Navigation 3 (nav3) — KMP status and recommendation
findings.guidance: androidx.navigation3:navigation3-runtime:1.1.2 (stable, May 19 2026) supports all KMP targets: Android, iOS, JVM Desktop, Linux, macOS, MinGW, JS, WASM. androidx.navigation3:navigation3-ui:1.1.2 is Android-ONLY — other platforms must implement their own NavDisplay. The CMP mirror is org.jetbrains.androidx.navigation3:navigation3-ui:1.0.0-alpha06 (alpha, from CMP 1.10.3). Google describes Nav3 as 'more than a new version — in a lot of ways it's a new library entirely' requiring a rewrite, not a migration. For existing apps on Nav2 (navigation-compose), no migration is required. For new CMP apps, Nav3 offers user-owned back stacks but requires implementing platform-specific NavDisplay for iOS/Desktop. For this project's migration, staying on org.jetbrains.androidx.navigation:navigation-compose:2.9.x is the lower-risk path. Sources: https://developer.android.com/jetpack/androidx/releases/navigation3 and https://kotlinlang.org/docs/multiplatform/compose-navigation-3.html

findings.topic: Navigation 3 — serialization requirement for iOS
findings.guidance: On iOS and Web (non-JVM), reflection is unavailable. Nav3 requires using the SavedStateConfiguration overload of rememberNavBackStack() with an explicit SerializersModule that registers polymorphic serializers for all NavKey subclasses. Example: polymorphic(NavKey::class) { subclass(RouteA::class, RouteA.serializer()) }. The annotation-based @Serializable on each route data class/object is the base requirement but not sufficient — explicit registration via SerializersModule is also needed. Source: https://kotlinlang.org/docs/multiplatform/compose-navigation-3.html

findings.topic: Material3 and Material3 Adaptive — CMP status
findings.guidance: In Compose Multiplatform, Material3 is accessed via org.jetbrains.compose.material3:material3 (bundled with the CMP BOM). As of CMP 1.10.3, material3 is at 1.10.0-alpha05 and material3-adaptive is at org.jetbrains.compose.material3.adaptive:adaptive*:1.3.0-alpha02. Material3 WindowSizeClass is available in commonMain via org.jetbrains.compose.material3:material3-window-size-class. The adaptive-navigation-suite is org.jetbrains.compose.material3:material3-adaptive-navigation-suite. iOS support for adaptive layouts is available but the adaptive artifacts remain in alpha as of mid-2026. For this project, using the CMP BOM (compose.bom from org.jetbrains.compose) is the correct approach — it resolves the right versions for all material3 sub-artifacts. Source: https://kotlinlang.org/docs/multiplatform/whats-new-compose-110.html

findings.topic: SavedState — KMP status
findings.guidance: androidx.savedstate:savedstate:1.5.0 (May 19 2026) is KMP-stable. Supports Android, iOS, JVM, Linux, macOS, MinGW, JS, WASM. androidx.savedstate:savedstate-compose:1.5.0 is also available. SavedStateHandle in commonMain is enabled via lifecycle-viewmodel-savedstate:2.10.0 (the SavedStateHandle class itself is in that artifact, not in the savedstate artifact). Source: https://developer.android.com/jetpack/androidx/releases/savedstate

findings.topic: androidx.collection and androidx.annotation — KMP status
findings.guidance: androidx.collection:collection:1.6.0 (March 11 2026, stable) — KMP supported since 1.3.0. Supports Android, JVM, iOS, watchOS, tvOS, Linux, macOS, WASM. Coordinates unchanged. androidx.annotation:annotation is published by Google as a fully multiplatform artifact and can be used in commonMain directly with unchanged coordinates. Neither library requires org.jetbrains mirrors. Source: https://developer.android.com/jetpack/androidx/releases/collection

findings.topic: Paging 3 — KMP status (not used but noted)
findings.guidance: androidx.paging:paging-common, paging-compose, paging-testing are KMP-stable as of version 3.4.0-rc01 (January 14 2026) targeting Android, JVM, iOS, Linux, macOS, MinGW, JS, WASM. Note: paging-compose for non-Android platforms uses the org.jetbrains.androidx.paging mirror. If EasyWatermark adds paging, use androidx.paging:paging-common in commonMain and the CMP mirror for paging-compose. Source: https://developer.android.com/jetpack/androidx/releases/paging

findings.topic: androidx vs org.jetbrains.androidx coordinate coexistence
findings.guidance: The org.jetbrains.androidx.* coordinates are publish-time wrappers: on Android, the Gradle CMP plugin resolves them to the original androidx.* artifacts. On other platforms they resolve to JetBrains-built artifacts. You do NOT need to manually put androidx.navigation:navigation-compose in androidMain alongside org.jetbrains.androidx.navigation:navigation-compose in commonMain — using the org.jetbrains.* version in commonMain alone is sufficient and correct. The official documentation states: 'Libraries published by JetBrains wrap Android artifacts together with artifacts for other platforms so you can seamlessly consume any and all of them in your multiplatform projects.' Libraries that Google publishes natively as KMP (Room, DataStore, Lifecycle, collection, annotation, savedstate, paging) keep their androidx.* coordinates and go directly in commonMain without any JetBrains mirror. The JetBrains mirror system is only needed for Compose UI, Navigation, and the Navigation3 UI artifact. Source: https://kotlinlang.org/docs/multiplatform/compose-multiplatform-jetpack-libraries.html

findings.topic: Which libraries need org.jetbrains.androidx.* coordinates vs keeping androidx.*
findings.guidance: USE org.jetbrains.androidx.* in commonMain: navigation-compose (org.jetbrains.androidx.navigation:navigation-compose:2.9.2), navigation3-ui (org.jetbrains.androidx.navigation3:navigation3-ui:1.0.0-alpha06), lifecycle-viewmodel-navigation3 (org.jetbrains.androidx.lifecycle:lifecycle-viewmodel-navigation3:2.10.0), Compose UI/Foundation/Material3 (org.jetbrains.compose.*). KEEP androidx.* coordinates in commonMain: room-runtime (2.8.4), datastore-preferences-core (1.2.1), lifecycle-viewmodel (2.10.0), lifecycle-runtime-compose (2.10.0), lifecycle-viewmodel-savedstate (2.10.0), savedstate (1.5.0), collection (1.6.0), annotation (latest), paging-common (3.4.x). Source: https://kotlinlang.org/docs/multiplatform/compose-multiplatform-jetpack-libraries.html

findings.topic: Minimum Kotlin and CMP version requirements
findings.guidance: Compose Multiplatform 1.10.3 requires Kotlin 2.2.20 minimum for native/web targets. This project is on Kotlin 2.3.20 which satisfies this. CMP 1.10.x ships with material3:1.10.0-alpha05 and navigation:2.9.2. The CMP 1.11.0-beta01 (March 2026) is in beta and includes further refinements. For this project targeting stable, CMP 1.10.3 + Kotlin 2.3.20 is the production-ready baseline. Source: https://kotlinlang.org/docs/multiplatform/whats-new-compose-110.html

mappings.solution: Keep androidx.room:room-runtime:2.8.4 in commonMain (no coordinate change needed). For this migration, staying on nav-compose 2.9.x is recommended. If Nav3 is adopted later: rewrite navigation layer, implement custom NavDisplay for iOS/Desktop, add SerializersModule with polymorphic serializers for all NavKey subtypes.

mappings.solution: For new apps: org.jetbrains.androidx.navigation3:navigation3-ui:1.0.0-alpha06 (commonMain) + androidx.navigation3:navigation3-runtime:1.1.2 (commonMain). Nav3 requires user-managed back stacks (List<NavKey>), custom NavDisplay per platform (android-only NavDisplay from navigation3-ui, custom for iOS/Desktop), and explicit polymorphic serialization. ecosystem.summary: As of June 2026, every Android-only dependency in EasyWatermark has a viable CMP replacement path. Coil 3 and FileKit are the two strongest direct replacements (stable / actively maintained). The biggest manual effort areas are: image compression (no drop-in KMP replacement for id.zelory:compressor — must write expect/actual over Skiko's encodeToData), Parcelable nav args (must migrate to @Serializable routes), and share-sheet (no common CMP API — must use expect/actual). All other needs have community libraries ranging from stable to late-beta. Peekaboo (Android+iOS only) is the weakest option and is outclassed by FileKit for this project's needs.

findings.topic: Coil 3 KMP image loading — coordinates and engine setup
findings.guidance: Migrate from io.coil-kt:coil (2.7) and Glide 5 to io.coil-kt.coil3:coil-compose:3.5.0 + io.coil-kt.coil3:coil-core:3.5.0. Network loading requires adding exactly one network artifact: io.coil-kt.coil3:coil-network-ktor3:3.5.0 (for Ktor 3.x) or coil-network-ktor2 for Ktor 2.x. Pair with platform-specific Ktor engines: ktor-client-okhttp (Android), ktor-client-darwin (iOS), ktor-client-java (JVM desktop). coil-svg is KMP-compatible and works on all targets including iOS, but a known upstream JetBrains Skia SVG parser crash on iOS was reported — verify it is resolved before shipping SVG decode on iOS. coil-gif and coil-video remain Android-only. Glide has no KMP support; remove entirely and consolidate on Coil 3.

findings.topic: Image / file picking + saving to photo library on iOS and desktop
findings.guidance: FileKit (io.github.vinceglb:filekit-dialogs-compose:0.14.1) is the recommended replacement for androidx.activity.result.PickVisualMedia. It wraps PickVisualMedia on Android, PHPickerViewController on iOS, NSOpenPanel on macOS, and XDG Portal on Linux. It supports picking single or multiple images, saving files to user-selected locations, and native camera capture on Android and iOS. A companion module filekit-coil integrates directly with Coil 3 for displaying PlatformFile images. Direct 'save to iOS Photos library' (PHPhotoLibrary.shared().performChanges) is not exposed in FileKit 0.14.1; that specific action still requires an expect/actual wrapper calling PHPhotoLibrary on iOS and MediaStore.Images.Media.insertImage on Android. Alternative calf-file-picker (com.mohamedrejeb.calf:calf-file-picker, latest v0.12.0) focuses on Android and iOS with some Desktop support, last released April 2026, active. Peekaboo (io.github.onseok:peekaboo-image-picker) targets Android + iOS only, last release v0.5.2 April 2024 — effectively stale and not recommended over FileKit.

findings.topic: Runtime permissions — photo library permission on iOS and Android
findings.guidance: Two maintained options: (1) moko-permissions (dev.icerock.moko:permissions:0.20.1, August 2025) — has explicit Permission.GALLERY module via dev.icerock.moko:permissions-gallery:0.20.1; provides PermissionsController with DeniedException / DeniedAlwaysException handling; Compose extensions via permissions-compose module; Android + iOS only. (2) calf-permissions (com.mohamedrejeb.calf:calf-permissions, v0.12.0, April 2026) — Compose Multiplatform API, Android + iOS focus with emerging Desktop support; modular per permission type. Community consensus on Kotlin Slack leans toward moko-permissions for photo-library specifically due to explicit gallery permission module. Writing thin expect/actual is also viable and keeps the dependency count low; the iOS actual is a single PHPhotoLibrary.requestAuthorization call.

findings.topic: Parcelable / @Parcelize in commonMain — nav args replacement
findings.guidance: The official Compose Multiplatform Navigation (androidx.navigation:navigation-compose, now multiplatform-capable as of Navigation 2.8+, current 2.9.7) uses @Serializable data classes and sealed interfaces from kotlinx.serialization as the nav-arg mechanism — this replaces @Parcelize entirely in shared code. Annotate route objects with @Serializable. Pass typed objects to navController.navigate(RouteObject(...)). Retrieve with backStackEntry.toRoute<RouteClass>(). In androidMain, @Parcelize can still be used for ViewModel state saved-state but must not appear in commonMain. Remove any use of @Parcelize from the shared nav-arg classes and replace with @Serializable. This is the official JetBrains-documented best practice.

findings.topic: EXIF metadata read/write across platforms
findings.guidance: Ashampoo Kim (com.ashampoo:kim:0.26.2, August 2025) is the only maintained KMP library offering both EXIF read and write. Platforms: JVM, Android, iOS, Windows, Linux, macOS, JS, WASM. Read+write for JPG, PNG (eXIf chunk), WebP, JXL. Read-only for HEIC, AVIF, TIFF, RAW formats (DNG, CR2, CR3, RAF, NEF, ARW, ORF, RW2). Reads via kotlin.ByteArray on all platforms; also accepts kotlinx.io Path, Ktor Source, java.io.File, NSData, and String path depending on target. EasyWatermark currently uses androidx.exifinterface — Kim is a direct replacement for JPEG EXIF read/write. For HEIC/AVIF (iOS camera output), Kim provides read-only metadata; writing HEIC EXIF still requires expect/actual over iOS ImageIO or CoreImage. No other actively maintained KMP EXIF library exists as of 2026.

findings.topic: Image compression/encoding with quality control in commonMain
findings.guidance: id.zelory:compressor (Android-only, no KMP support, last meaningful update 2021) has no KMP analogue — it must be replaced manually. The CMP-available mechanism is Skiko's org.jetbrains.skia.Image.encodeToData(EncodedImageFormat.JPEG, quality: Int): Data? where quality is 0–100 (same semantics as Android's Bitmap.compress). Supported encode formats via Skiko include JPEG, PNG, WEBP (lossless and lossy). Flow: obtain ImageBitmap → convert to org.jetbrains.skia.Bitmap via asSkiaBitmap() (available in commonMain via compose-ui) → org.jetbrains.skia.Image.makeFromBitmap(bitmap) → image.encodeToData(EncodedImageFormat.JPEG, quality). This works on Android, iOS (Skiko), and Desktop (Skiko). Progressive JPEG encoding is not supported by Skia/Skiko. On Android only, you may still call android.graphics.Bitmap.compress in androidMain for maximum compatibility. FileKit 0.14.1 also exposes FileKit.compressImage() with quality and dimension parameters as a higher-level cross-platform option.

findings.topic: Palette / dominant-color extraction replacing androidx.palette
findings.guidance: Two KMP libraries available: (1) kmpalette (com.kmpalette:kmpalette-core:3.1.0 stable, 4.0.0-beta02 with new group com.materialkolor.palette:core) — a direct port of androidx.palette for Compose Multiplatform. Supports Android, iOS, Desktop, JS, WASM. Provides DominantColorState and PaletteState composable state holders via rememberDominantColorState and rememberPaletteState. Extension modules for network and base64 image sources. Stable 3.1.0 is the safe choice; 4.0.0-beta02 renames the group ID to materialkolor.palette. (2) MaterialKolor (com.materialkolor:material-kolor:4.1.1, February 2026) — generates Material3 dynamic ColorScheme from a seed color; it is complementary to kmpalette, not a replacement (does theme generation, not palette extraction from images). Recommended: use kmpalette-core:3.1.0 for the androidx.palette use cases in EasyWatermark.

findings.topic: Color picker Composable for CMP replacing skydoves colorpickerview (View-based)
findings.guidance: skydoves/colorpicker-compose (com.github.skydoves:colorpicker-compose:1.2.0) is a Kotlin Multiplatform Compose library — not the legacy View-based colorpickerview. It supports Android, iOS (arm64, iosSimulatorArm64), macOS (arm64), JVM Desktop, JS, and WASM. Provides ImageColorPicker (sample colors from any image by tap) and HsvColorPicker (HSV palette), plus BrightnessSlider and AlphaSlider composables. This is a direct drop-in for the existing skydoves dependency in EasyWatermark (the project already uses the skydoves ecosystem). EasyWatermark's current dependency is colorpickerview (View-based, Android-only); replacing it with colorpicker-compose:1.2.0 requires adapting from View callbacks to Compose state/lambda patterns but is otherwise straightforward.

findings.topic: Haptics in CMP common code
findings.guidance: LocalHapticFeedback.current is available in commonMain via androidx.compose.ui and works on Android and Desktop. On iOS, long-press haptic feedback via LocalHapticFeedback was not functional (GitHub issue #4598 in compose-multiplatform). As of CMP 1.8+ the iOS haptic implementation was improved (release notes reference haptic tick fixes for SegmentFrequentTick/SegmentTick). For production-quality haptics on iOS, wrapping UIImpactFeedbackGenerator via an expect/actual is still the safest path. The LocalHapticFeedback common API is correct to call everywhere — just be aware iOS may silently no-op on some feedback types.

findings.topic: Clipboard in CMP common code
findings.guidance: LocalClipboardManager (ClipboardManager interface) is available in commonMain but deprecated for web. The replacement is the new Clipboard interface (adopted from Jetpack Compose) which supports suspend functions and all CMP targets including web (issue CMP-7624 tracks remaining gaps). For EasyWatermark's needs (copy text to clipboard): use LocalClipboardManager.current.setText(AnnotatedString(...)) which works on Android, iOS, and Desktop in CMP 1.8+. For full web compatibility, migrate to the new Clipboard suspend API when available.

findings.topic: Share sheet / ACTION_SEND equivalent in CMP
findings.guidance: There is no common CMP API for share sheets as of June 2026. The expect/actual pattern is required. Android actual: Intent(Intent.ACTION_SEND) with FileProvider URI for files or plain text. iOS actual: UIActivityViewController. Desktop actual: platform-specific clipboard copy or file-system write. A community article (Medium, March 2026) demonstrates this pattern with a ShareManager expect class in commonMain. No third-party KMP library wraps this with maintained status.

findings.topic: Open URL / external browser in CMP
findings.guidance: LocalUriHandler.current.openUri(url) is the common CMP API and works across Android, iOS, and Desktop without expect/actual. On iOS 18+ a crash was reported when using the UIApplication.openURL path internally; this was fixed in CMP 1.7.0-rc01. For EasyWatermark's About screen link navigation, LocalUriHandler is sufficient and idiomatic.

findings.topic: Crash reporting and analytics in KMP
findings.guidance: Sentry KMP SDK (io.sentry:sentry-kotlin-multiplatform:0.27.0, released June 3, 2026) is the most mature cross-platform crash reporting option. Supports Android, iOS, macOS, JVM (desktop). JS/WASM/Linux/Windows targets are stubbed (no-op). Production-ready per Sentry's own classification. For Firebase Crashlytics: no official KMP SDK exists; Kotlin crashes from commonMain on iOS require extra instrumentation via setUnhandledExceptionHook plus CrashKiOS (touchlab) for symbolicated stack traces. EasyWatermark does not appear to use crash reporting currently; if added, Sentry KMP is the lowest-friction cross-platform solution.
