cmpGraphics.summary: Research into Compose Multiplatform (CMP) graphics capabilities for a watermark engine in commonMain, as of June 2026 (latest stable CMP version: 1.11.1, with 1.12.0-alpha available; Skia milestone 144 in 1.11.0, m148 in 1.12.0-alpha). The watermark engine requirements -- decode large photos, draw rotated tiled text/image overlays, render consistently for preview and export, encode to JPEG/PNG/WebP -- expose a significant split between what is natively in commonMain versus what requires expect/actual. The critical constraint is that Skiko APIs (org.jetbrains.skia.*) are NOT accessible from commonMain: they must live in a non-Android (iosMain/desktopMain/skikoCommonMain) source set, while Android requires BitmapFactory / Bitmap.compress. Encoding to JPEG/PNG/WebP is the most significant expect/actual boundary. Canvas offscreen drawing via CanvasDrawScope + ImageBitmap(width,height) is a confirmed common API. TextMeasurer/drawText is common but requires a Composable context (font resolver). ImageShader with TileMode.Repeated is in common. GraphicsLayer.record/toImageBitmap is in commonMain as an expect class but requires an active Compose scene. Text rendering uses different backends on Android (Minikin/HarfBuzz + Skia rasterization) versus iOS/desktop (SkParagraph), causing non-pixel-identical cross-platform text output even for the same bundled font. iOS memory pressure from 50MP bitmaps is a real concern under Kotlin/Native GC; tile-based rendering is the standard mitigation.

findings.topic: Decode: ByteArray to ImageBitmap in commonMain
findings.guidance: CMP 1.7.0 added ByteArray.decodeToImageBitmap() as a RESOURCE utility function in commonMain (androidx.compose.ui.res or the multiplatform resources module), supporting JPEG, PNG, BMP, and WEBP decode. This is confirmed in the official 1.7.3 what-is-new docs. HOWEVER, this decode function wraps platform decoders and provides NO downsampling options (no BitmapFactory.Options.inSampleSize equivalent in common code). For direct ByteArray decode without the resource system, the split remains: Android uses BitmapFactory.decodeByteArray(bytes, 0, bytes.size).asImageBitmap() in androidMain; iOS/desktop uses org.jetbrains.skia.Image.makeFromEncoded(bytes).toComposeImageBitmap() in iosMain/desktopMain. The Skiko function makeFromEncoded is in org.jetbrains.skia package which is commonMain in the skiko repo source tree BUT is NOT accessible from your CMP commonMain: placing it there causes 'Could not find skia' compilation errors on Android -- it must be in skikoCommonMain or per-platform. Recommended pattern: define expect fun ByteArray.toImageBitmap(): ImageBitmap in commonMain with actual implementations per platform. For CMP 1.11.x the decodeToImageBitmap() extension on ByteArray from the multiplatform resources usage API (kotlinlang.org/docs/multiplatform/compose-multiplatform-resources-usage.html) is the cleanest common path, but it does not support downsampling for huge images.

findings.topic: Downsampling large photos on decode (preview path)
findings.guidance: There is NO common downsampling API in CMP. On Android, BitmapFactory.Options with inSampleSize and inJustDecodeBounds lets you decode a 50MP photo at 1/8th resolution for preview. On iOS/desktop via Skiko, org.jetbrains.skia.Image.makeFromEncoded decodes at full resolution with no built-in subsampling; you must manually scale after decode using Canvas operations or use Coil 3 (coil-kt/coil, multiplatform-aware) which handles downsampling per platform internally. For the preview path in a watermark app, the recommended approach is: (1) use Coil 3 AsyncImage for display (it handles platform-specific downsampling transparently), (2) for the offscreen engine, decode a downsampled version via expect/actual for the preview canvas (Android: BitmapFactory inSampleSize; iOS: decode full then scale to screen resolution using SkiaImage.makeRaster or equivalent). Coil 3 is KMP-ready as of 3.0+ and uses Skiko on non-Android platforms.

findings.topic: Offscreen rendering: Canvas(ImageBitmap) + CanvasDrawScope in commonMain
findings.guidance: Confirmed common API. The pattern ImageBitmap(width, height) allocates an offscreen bitmap (ARGB_8888), Canvas(imageBitmap) wraps it, and CanvasDrawScope().draw(density, layoutDirection, canvas, size) { ... } executes DrawScope operations into it without any Composable context. This is in androidx.compose.ui.graphics (commonMain). Multiple community articles confirm this works in CMP commonMain for offscreen image processing. There is no documented hard pixel limit on allocation size in the CMP API, but practical limits are OS-imposed: iOS will OOM on a 50MP (e.g., 8192x6144) ARGB_8888 bitmap which requires ~192 MB raw. The allocation itself will succeed until the OS kills the process. For full-resolution export of 50MP images, tile-based processing (render the watermark tile, then stamp it across the full-resolution image in chunks) is the recommended mitigation.

findings.topic: GraphicsLayer.record + toImageBitmap as alternative for offscreen export
findings.guidance: GraphicsLayer is an expect class defined in commonMain (androidx.compose.ui.graphics.layer.GraphicsLayer, confirmed in AOSP source at android.googlesource.com). It exposes suspend fun toImageBitmap(): ImageBitmap and record(density, layoutDirection, size, block: DrawScope.() -> Unit). As of CMP 1.7.0 it is available across platforms. CRITICAL LIMITATION for headless export: GraphicsLayer requires an active Compose rendering scene (a window/surface) to function correctly -- it cannot be used in a background coroutine without an attached ComposeOwner/composition. The community has confirmed that to capture at full resolution without displaying, you need the composable to be in the composition tree (e.g., use a hidden surface or presentation). For a watermark export engine that runs entirely in background without UI, CanvasDrawScope + ImageBitmap is more appropriate than GraphicsLayer. GraphicsLayer is better for capture-what-is-displayed patterns.

findings.topic: Text: TextMeasurer and drawText in commonMain
findings.guidance: TextMeasurer is in androidx.compose.ui.text (commonMain) and DrawScope.drawText(textMeasurer, text, topLeft, style) is a common API. CONSTRAINT: TextMeasurer requires LocalFontFamilyResolver and LocalLayoutDirection composition locals. When used in an offscreen CanvasDrawScope context (outside a Composable), you must manually supply a FontFamilyResolver (createFontFamilyResolver() on JVM/desktop, platform-specific on iOS) and LayoutDirection. A known GitHub issue (#3289) documents that using rememberTextMeasurer() outside a Window/Composable throws. Workaround: construct TextMeasurer(createFontFamilyResolver(context), density, LayoutDirection.Ltr) directly with explicit parameters -- the constructor is available but not @Composable. For font loading, use the CMP multiplatform resources Font() API (Res.font.*) which loads fonts from commonMain/composeResources and is the recommended cross-platform approach since CMP 1.6.0.

findings.topic: Cross-platform text rendering fidelity (watermark identity across platforms)
findings.guidance: CMP does NOT guarantee pixel-identical text rendering across platforms. The root cause is a backend split: Android Jetpack Compose uses Minikin for text shaping/layout with Skia for glyph rasterization (the Android text pipeline), while iOS and desktop Compose use SkParagraph (Skia's paragraph module) for both shaping and rasterization. Even when using the SAME bundled font (loaded via Compose resources), you will observe: (1) sub-pixel antialiasing differences (Android uses LCD subpixel, iOS/desktop use grayscale AA by default on Metal); (2) slight kerning/letter-spacing differences due to different ICU and shaping engine versions; (3) line-height behavior that differs (CMP 1.8.x standardized LineHeightStyle.Alignment across platforms, which reduces one class of difference). JetBrains official docs (compose-platform-specifics.html) state explicitly: 'Compose Multiplatform doesn't guarantee pixel-perfect correspondence between different platforms.' For a watermark that must look 'identically-ish': use bundled fonts (not system fonts), use sp-based sizing, accept ~1-3px line metric differences. If pixel-perfect cross-platform text is required (e.g., for exact positioning of a copyright stamp), the only reliable approach is to render text via the Skiko SkParagraph API directly on all platforms (bypassing Compose text) or accept the difference.

findings.topic: Tiling: ImageShader with TileMode.Repeated + rotation in commonMain DrawScope
findings.guidance: ImageShader(imageBitmap, tileModeX = TileMode.Repeated, tileModeY = TileMode.Repeated) is a common API in androidx.compose.ui.graphics. Creating a ShaderBrush(ImageShader(...)) and using it in DrawScope.drawRect() or Modifier.background() tiles the image. This is confirmed at composables.com/docs/androidx.compose.ui/ui-graphics/functions/ImageShader. For ROTATION of the tiled pattern (diagonal watermark tile), ImageShader itself takes no Matrix parameter in its Compose wrapper API. The approach is: (1) use DrawScope.rotate(degrees) { drawRect(brush = ShaderBrush(ImageShader(...))) } to rotate the entire drawing context before applying the tiled brush -- this achieves diagonal tiling for a watermark effect; OR (2) in CMP 1.11.0+, the non-Android Shader type was changed to a dedicated Compose wrapper (breaking change), so raw Skia-shader-based matrix transforms must use SkShader.asComposeShader() to wrap, with the underlying skiaShader property exposing the native type if needed. The DrawScope.rotate() approach is the simplest and works cross-platform without touching Skia internals.

findings.topic: Encode: ImageBitmap to JPEG/PNG/WebP bytes in commonMain
findings.guidance: There is NO common encoding API in CMP. Encoding is a required expect/actual boundary. The standard community-confirmed patterns are: ANDROID (androidMain): imageBitmap.asAndroidBitmap().let { bmp -> ByteArrayOutputStream().also { bmp.compress(Bitmap.CompressFormat.JPEG, quality, it) }.toByteArray() }. Non-ANDROID (iosMain / desktopMain / skikoCommonMain): org.jetbrains.skia.Image.makeFromBitmap(imageBitmap.asSkiaBitmap()).encodeToData(EncodedImageFormat.JPEG, quality)?.bytes. The Skiko encodeToData supports EncodedImageFormat.JPEG, PNG, and WEBP (confirmed in skiko/src/commonMain/kotlin/org/jetbrains/skia/Image.kt at JetBrains/skiko). WebP encode via Skia/Skiko is supported on iOS and desktop (Skia has had WebP encode via libwebp since early milestones). Android WebP encode via Bitmap.compress is supported from API 30+ for lossy WebP with quality; API 30+ for lossless. For min-API < 30 on Android, use Bitmap.CompressFormat.WEBP (deprecated but functional, always lossy) or require API 30. The asSkiaBitmap() and asAndroidBitmap() extensions are platform-specific and not in commonMain. A recommended abstraction: define expect fun ImageBitmap.encodeToBytes(format: ImageFormat, quality: Int): ByteArray in commonMain with actual implementations per platform.

findings.topic: WebP encode support on iOS/desktop via Skiko
findings.guidance: Confirmed via Skiko source: org.jetbrains.skia.Image.encodeToData(EncodedImageFormat.WEBP, quality) is available in skiko commonMain and works on iOS (arm64/x64) and desktop (JVM macOS/Linux/Windows). Skia bundles libwebp. The same function also supports JPEG and PNG. On macOS, additional formats (ICO, BMP, GIF) are available. Quality parameter maps to WebP quality (0-100). This is the same Skia WebP encoder used in Chrome. One historical issue (CMP issue #2480 from 2022) questioned whether painterResource() could load WebP on iOS -- this was about decode support in the resource system, not encode, and was resolved as WebP decode is supported via Skia on iOS. Encode has no separate issue and is expected to work.

findings.topic: Memory: 50MP photos on iOS (Kotlin/Native, ImageBitmap backing)
findings.guidance: A 50MP image (e.g., 8736x5824 pixels from an iPhone 15 Pro Max 48MP sensor or a medium-format camera) decoded to ARGB_8888 requires approximately 200MB of RAM. Kotlin/Native on iOS uses a tracing GC (since Kotlin 1.7.20), not reference counting. This means large Skia Bitmap objects backing ImageBitmap may not be released promptly between frames if references exist. Known issues: (1) KT-61763 / discuss.kotlinlang.org/t/27347 documents a UIImage→Kotlin boundary memory spike (600MB+ during processing); (2) CMP issue #4912 documents general memory/CPU issues on iOS with Compose. Mitigations for the watermark engine: (a) Never hold the full-resolution ImageBitmap in memory longer than necessary -- decode, stamp watermark, encode, release; (b) For preview: always downsample to screen resolution before creating ImageBitmap (expect/actual decode with inSampleSize on Android, manual scale on iOS); (c) For export of very large images: implement tile-based watermark stamping -- decode a tile (e.g., 2048x2048), draw watermark overlay on tile, encode tile, move to next tile, stitch or use streaming JPEG encoder; (d) Explicitly call System.gc() (JVM) or kotlin.native.internal.GC.collect() (Native) after releasing large bitmaps; (e) Consider using the ZoomImage library (panpf/zoomimage, CMP-compatible) for the preview path as it implements subsampling natively across platforms.

findings.topic: Performance: Skiko rendering on iOS Metal for pinch-zoom preview of large bitmaps
findings.guidance: CMP on iOS uses Skia → Metal pipeline. As of CMP 1.8.0 (May 2025), iOS is declared stable and production-ready. CMP 1.8.0 introduced concurrent rendering on iOS (offloading to a dedicated render thread) as opt-in; CMP 1.11.0 made it the DEFAULT. This significantly improves pinch-zoom responsiveness on large bitmaps. Practical notes: (1) For a pinch-zoom preview of a watermarked photo, always display a downsampled ImageBitmap (not the full 50MP); use a zoomable composable that lazily renders detail tiles (ZoomImage library supports this in CMP). (2) Metal's tile memory architecture means very large single-draw textures can be slow -- prefer drawing at the screen's physical resolution, not the photo's native resolution. (3) Skia m144 (CMP 1.11.0) includes rendering improvements. (4) There is a known bug fix in compose-multiplatform-core PR #554 for incorrect Skiko render target on iOS Metal (merged, present in current releases). (5) 120Hz ProMotion displays are fully supported; the render thread change in 1.11.0 keeps the UI thread free for input, which is essential for smooth pinch-zoom.

findings.topic: CMP version context and Skia milestone
findings.guidance: As of June 2026: CMP 1.11.1 is the latest stable release (requires Kotlin 2.2+). CMP 1.12.0-alpha01 is the preview (Skia m148). CMP 1.11.0 uses Skia m144. The non-Android Shader breaking change (Shader becomes a Compose wrapper, not a direct Skia typealias) landed in 1.11.0 -- any code using Paint.asFrameworkPaint() must migrate to Paint.skiaPaint; Canvas.nativeCanvas to Canvas.skiaCanvas; RenderEffect.asSkiaImageFilter() to RenderEffect.skiaImageFilter. This affects how the watermark engine accesses low-level Skia paint and canvas APIs from non-commonMain source sets.

mappings.solution: commonMain: ByteArray.decodeToImageBitmap() (CMP resource API, no downsampling) OR expect/actual: androidMain BitmapFactory + asImageBitmap(), iosMain/desktopMain org.jetbrains.skia.Image.makeFromEncoded(bytes).toComposeImageBitmap()
mappings.notes: decodeToImageBitmap() is official CMP API since 1.7.0. Skiko Image.makeFromEncoded must not be in commonMain (compile error on Android).

mappings.need: Offscreen canvas drawing for watermark compositing
mappings.solution: commonMain: val bmp = ImageBitmap(w, h); val canvas = Canvas(bmp); CanvasDrawScope().draw(density, LayoutDirection.Ltr, canvas, Size(w.f, h.f)) { /* drawImage, drawText, drawRect with ShaderBrush */ }
mappings.notes: All APIs confirmed in commonMain. No Composable context required. CanvasDrawScope is in androidx.compose.ui.graphics.drawscope.

mappings.current: Custom path tiling + canvas.rotate() in WaterMarkImageView
mappings.solution: commonMain: ImageShader(tile, TileMode.Repeated, TileMode.Repeated) wrapped in ShaderBrush; use DrawScope.rotate(angle) { drawRect(brush) } for diagonal tiling. For text tiles: pre-render text to a small ImageBitmap via CanvasDrawScope, then use that as the ImageShader source.
mappings.notes: ImageShader is common. Rotation via DrawScope.rotate() is common. CMP 1.11.0 Shader type change: use SkShader.asComposeShader() if going below the Compose layer.

mappings.current: Paint.drawText on Android Canvas in WaterMarkImageView
mappings.solution: commonMain: TextMeasurer + DrawScope.drawText(). Requires providing FontFamilyResolver and LayoutDirection explicitly when used outside Composable. Load fonts via CMP resources (Res.font.*) for cross-platform consistency.
mappings.notes: Cross-platform text is NOT pixel-identical. Android uses Minikin+Skia; iOS/desktop use SkParagraph. Expect ~1-3px differences in glyph metrics. Use bundled fonts, not system fonts.

mappings.solution: expect/actual required. androidMain: imageBitmap.asAndroidBitmap().compress(...). iosMain/desktopMain: imageBitmap.asSkiaBitmap() then org.jetbrains.skia.Image.makeFromBitmap(skiaBitmap).encodeToData(EncodedImageFormat.JPEG/PNG/WEBP, quality)?.bytes
mappings.notes: No common encode API exists in CMP. Skiko supports JPEG, PNG, WebP on iOS and desktop. Android WebP with quality requires API 30+.

mappings.need: Large photo memory management on iOS
mappings.current: Android only, memory managed by JVM GC
mappings.solution: Tile-based processing: never load full 50MP as a single ImageBitmap on iOS. Decode preview at screen resolution (expect/actual downsample). For export: process in 2048x2048 tiles. Explicitly trigger GC after large bitmap release. Consider ZoomImage (panpf/zoomimage) for preview subsampling.
mappings.notes: Kotlin/Native tracing GC does not release Skia backing memory as promptly as Android. Known issue KT-61763. CMP issue #4912 documents iOS memory pressure.

officialSkills.summary: Analysis of the official android/skills GitHub repository (last-updated dates in skill files range from 2026-04-01 to 2026-06-08). Three skill groups are directly relevant to the EasyWatermark CMP migration: (1) jetpack-compose/migration/migrate-xml-views-to-jetpack-compose — a 10-step structured workflow for converting legacy Views/XML to Compose, with concrete rules on state management, theming, interoperability APIs, reusable composable design, and visual validation; (2) navigation/navigation-3 — prescribes NavDisplay + NavEntry + mutable-list-as-backstack replacing NavHost + NavController, with a full migration guide from Navigation 2; it makes no mention of KMP/multiplatform support and the migration guide explicitly requires compileSdk 36 and is marked "designed exclusively for Compose (Android)"; (3) several other skills (adaptive, edge-to-edge, testing-setup, agp-9-upgrade, theming/styles) are relevant to the migration pipeline. The agp-9-upgrade skill explicitly states "Do not use this skill for migrating Kotlin Multiplatform (KMP) projects." Install commands use the android CLI tool from dl.google.com.

findings.topic: XML-to-Compose migration: 10-step structured workflow
findings.guidance: The migrate-xml-views-to-jetpack-compose skill mandates a 10-step process: (1) identify optimal XML candidate, (2) audit project/layout, (3) create a plan, (4) capture baseline screenshot of XML UI, (5) set up Compose dependencies and compiler, (6) set up minimal Compose theming (do NOT migrate the entire theme — only what the candidate needs), (7) migrate XML to Compose with a mandatory @Preview, (8) replace usages using Compose-in-Views or Views-in-Compose interop APIs, (9) validate visually against baseline screenshot, (10) delete migrated XML. For EasyWatermark, WaterMarkImageView is the prime candidate — currently embedded via AndroidView in EditorScreen, it should be the last thing replaced after all surrounding Compose scaffolding is stable.

findings.topic: XML-to-Compose migration: do not migrate entire theme at once
findings.guidance: Skill constraint (Step 6): 'Do not migrate the entire theme. Implement only the minimum theming required for the specific XML candidate. Maintain original XML themes for interoperability.' This means while migrating WaterMarkImageView, only expose the color/dimension tokens it actually uses into MaterialTheme; do not port all app theme resources in one pass.

findings.topic: XML-to-Compose migration: Views-in-Compose interop for legacy custom views
findings.guidance: Step 8 of the migration skill explicitly provides two references: 'Compose in Views' (ComposeView, AbstractComposeView) and 'Views in Compose' (AndroidView/AndroidViewBinding). For WaterMarkImageView — a custom View that owns its own Canvas drawing — the skill endorses continuing to wrap it with AndroidView until a full Compose Canvas replacement is ready. This is the correct incremental path rather than a big-bang rewrite.

findings.topic: XML-to-Compose migration: reusable composable design and Modifier convention
findings.guidance: xml-layout-migration.md rule: every migrated component that serves as a design-system foundation must become a standalone @Composable (not inlined), must expose data parameters plus a Modifier parameter for layout customization, and must use MaterialTheme tokens (colorScheme, typography, shapes) rather than hard-coded values. For EditorScreen's slider/panel UI, each control panel should be its own @Composable with a Modifier slot, hoisting state up to the screen-level composable or ViewModel.

findings.topic: XML-to-Compose migration: state hoisting and consistency analysis
findings.guidance: analysis-of-the-project-and-layout.md mandates: scan all existing @Composable functions to identify the project's established state-hoisting pattern before writing new code; align with it rather than inventing a new one. For EditorScreen this means following whatever pattern MainViewModel + EditorScreen already use (StateFlow -> collectAsStateWithLifecycle). Do not introduce a second state-management layer.

findings.topic: XML-to-Compose migration: preview is mandatory
findings.guidance: Step 7 explicitly states 'You must include a Compose Preview for the newly created composable to facilitate visual verification.' For an image-editor screen with sliders, create @Preview variants at compact/medium/expanded widths. The adaptive skill reinforces this with a FormFactorPreviews annotation covering Phone/Foldable/Tablet/Desktop device specs.

findings.topic: Navigation 3: NavDisplay replaces NavHost; backstack is plain mutable state list
findings.guidance: Navigation 3 (nav3) replaces NavHost+NavController with NavDisplay + a MutableList<NavKey> as the backstack. To navigate forward: add to the list. To go back: removeLastOrNull(). NavDisplay's entryProvider lambda resolves a NavKey to a NavEntry. There is no NavGraph DSL — destinations are resolved in a when() block or via entryProvider { entry<RouteType> { } } DSL. The migration guide's Step 6 code is: NavDisplay(entries = navigationState.toEntries(entryProvider), onBack = { navigator.goBack() }, sceneStrategies = remember { listOf(DialogSceneStrategy()) }). EasyWatermark's ComposeMainActivity currently uses navigation-compose 2.9.7; migrating to nav3 requires replacing NavHost with NavDisplay and NavController with a NavigationState/Navigator pair.

findings.topic: Navigation 3: routes must implement NavKey; compileSdk 36 required
findings.guidance: Migration guide Step 1: add androidx.navigation3:navigation3-runtime:1.0.0 and androidx.navigation3:navigation3-ui:1.0.0. Step 2: every route data class/object must implement NavKey (and carry @Serializable). The guide requires compileSdk 36 and minSdk 23. EasyWatermark's current routes (LaunchScreen, GalleryDialog, EditorScreen nav args) must be refactored to @Serializable data objects/classes : NavKey. The nav3 version in the migration guide references 1.0.0 — distinct from the navigation-compose 2.9.7 currently in use.

findings.topic: Navigation 3: backstack is state — unidirectional data flow architecture
findings.guidance: The migration guide mandates creating a NavigationState holder (rememberNavBackStack per top-level route, rememberSerializable for current top-level route) and a Navigator class that mutates it. NavDisplay observes NavigationState and reacts. This is explicitly called out as following Unidirectional Data Flow. For EasyWatermark this means the LaunchScreen->EditorScreen navigation state should live in a state holder, not be driven by imperative NavController.navigate() calls scattered across composables.

findings.topic: Navigation 3: Scenes API for adaptive multi-pane layouts (list-detail, bottom sheet, dialog)
findings.guidance: Navigation 3 replaces the adaptive scaffold approach (ListDetailPaneScaffold) with a SceneStrategy system passed to NavDisplay via sceneStrategies. Dialog destinations get metadata = DialogSceneStrategy.dialog(). List-detail uses ListDetailSceneStrategy from adaptive-navigation3 lib. The adaptive skill (Step 3) says 'You MUST use the Navigation 3 SceneStrategy approach. Do not use ListDetailPaneScaffold or SupportingPaneScaffold.' SaveExportSheet in EasyWatermark should use a BottomSheetSceneStrategy (must be copied from the nav3-recipes repo as it is not in the core lib).

findings.topic: Navigation 3: KMP/multiplatform readiness — NOT addressed in the skill
findings.guidance: The navigation/navigation-3 SKILL.md and its migration-guide.md reference make zero mentions of Kotlin Multiplatform, iOS, or desktop targets. The index.md describes Navigation 3 as 'designed to work with Compose' with no platform qualifier, but all dependency coordinates are androidx.navigation3 (Android-scoped artifacts). As of the skill's last-updated date of 2026-06-02, the skill does not prescribe or endorse Navigation 3 as KMP-ready. For a CMP migration targeting iOS+Desktop, plan for a navigation abstraction layer or a different CMP-compatible navigation library (e.g. Decompose, Voyager, or the experimental navigation-compose-multiplatform) rather than assuming nav3 works cross-platform.

findings.topic: Navigation 3: unsupported features — deep links, nested nav >1 level, shared destinations
findings.guidance: Migration guide 'Unsupported features' section: more than one level of nested navigation, shared destinations (screens that can move between backstacks), custom destination types, and deep links are explicitly not covered. EasyWatermark uses deep-link-like behavior via ACTION_SEND in legacy MainActivity; this flow must be kept on legacy MainActivity or handled outside of nav3 until deep link support is added. Do not attempt to migrate the share-in flow into nav3 as part of the initial migration.

findings.topic: Navigation 3: migration from nav2 is atomic, not incremental
findings.guidance: Migration guide Assumptions section: 'You want to perform the migration from Navigation 2 to Navigation 3 in a single, atomic change. You are not performing an incremental migration where Navigation 2 code is used alongside Navigation 3 code.' For EasyWatermark (currently on navigation-compose 2.9.7 in feat/migrate_to_compose), the nav3 migration should be a dedicated branch/PR that replaces all NavHost/NavController usage in ComposeMainActivity at once, not done screen-by-screen alongside other Compose work.

findings.topic: edge-to-edge skill: Scaffold innerPadding must be consumed, not double-applied
findings.guidance: The edge-to-edge SKILL.md (last-updated 2026-04-01) prescribes: (1) call enableEdgeToEdge() before setContent in every Activity; (2) use Scaffold { innerPadding -> ... } and pass innerPadding to contentPadding of scrollable components, not as Modifier.padding() on a parent container (that clips content). The skill warns that Modifier.imePadding() combined with contentWindowInsets = WindowInsets.safeDrawing causes double padding. It also prescribes Modifier.fitInside(WindowInsetsRulers.Ime.current) as the preferred IME handling. For EditorScreen, which has a canvas + bottom panel, ensure the bottom panel uses safeDrawingPadding() or Scaffold innerPadding, and do NOT apply safeDrawingPadding() to a NavigationSuiteScaffold parent.

findings.topic: edge-to-edge skill: NavigationSuiteScaffold does not propagate PaddingValues to content
findings.guidance: Adaptive Scaffolds section: 'NavigationSuiteScaffold does not propagate PaddingValues to their inner contents. You MUST apply insets to individual screens or components.' Do NOT apply safeDrawingPadding to the NavigationSuiteScaffold wrapper. If EasyWatermark adopts NavigationSuiteScaffold (recommended by the adaptive skill for tablet/foldable), each screen inside it must manage its own insets independently.

findings.topic: testing-setup skill: multiplatform DI framework recommendation
findings.guidance: testing-setup SKILL.md Step 2: 'If there is no Dependency Injection framework, install one: if it is a multiplatform application, ask the user whether they want to install Koin, or kotlin-inject. If it is not multiplatform, install Hilt.' EasyWatermark already uses Koin 4.2.1, which is the correct choice for CMP. No DI migration needed. However, the skill requires adding Koin instrumented testing dependencies with kspAndroidTest configuration and a custom TestRunner.

findings.topic: testing-setup skill: screenshot tests at 9 form-factor sizes; Compose Preview Screenshot Testing preferred
findings.guidance: Step 8: screen-level screenshot tests must cover 9 size combinations (compact/medium/expanded width x compact/medium/expanded height: 400/610/900 dp x 400/500/1000 dp) plus font-scale 1.5 variant. The preferred local tool is the Compose Preview Screenshot Testing tool (not Paparazzi). For device-based screenshot tests, use Dropshots. The adaptive skill adds a @FormFactorPreviews annotation covering Phone/Foldable/Tablet/Desktop. For EditorScreen with its zoomable canvas + slider panels, these multi-size tests are essential before a CMP migration to catch viewport/inset regressions.

findings.topic: testing-setup skill: Robolectric runs Compose UI tests locally; androidTest reserved for instrumented
findings.guidance: Step 6: 'Espresso or Compose UI tests live in the test sourceset because they will be run with Robolectric. If instrumented tests are requested, put them in the androidTest sourceset.' Also Step 5: 'Don't create unit tests for Activities, Compose layouts, or dependency injection configuration files.' For EasyWatermark this means UI tests for EditorScreen go in the test/ (Robolectric) sourceset, not androidTest/, unless device-specific behavior (camera, insets) needs testing.

findings.topic: agp-9-upgrade skill: explicitly unsupported for KMP projects
findings.guidance: agp-9-upgrade SKILL.md description: 'Do not use this skill for migrating Kotlin Multiplatform (KMP) projects.' and in the Requirements section: 'Do not use this skill for KMP projects, as they are unsupported.' EasyWatermark is currently a pure Android app (AGP 8.13.2); the AGP 9 upgrade should be completed BEFORE converting to a KMP/CMP project structure, using this skill for the Android-only codebase. Once KMP modules are introduced, further AGP changes must be done manually or with KMP-specific guidance.

findings.topic: agp-9-upgrade skill: KSP must be 2.3.6+; Hilt must be 2.59.2+ for AGP 9
findings.guidance: Step 1: 'If KSP is used, ensure version 2.3.6 or higher. If Hilt is used, ensure version 2.59.2 or higher.' EasyWatermark uses Koin (not Hilt) so the Hilt constraint does not apply, but KSP version must be verified. The skill also requires migrating kapt to KSP (Step 4) and adopting the new AGP 9 DSL (Step 3). Paparazzi v2.0.0-alpha04 and lower has issues with AGP 9 (documented in references/paparazzi-gradle-9.md).

findings.topic: adaptive skill: requires full Compose + Navigation 3 before adaptive work
findings.guidance: adaptive SKILL.md Prerequisites: 'The app must use Compose for all screens. If it's still using Fragments or Views, suggest using the XML to Compose skill to migrate those screens. Use Jetpack Navigation 3. If it doesn't, suggest the Navigation 3 skill to migrate the app.' This sets a hard prerequisite order for EasyWatermark: (1) complete Compose migration of WaterMarkImageView, (2) migrate to nav3, (3) then apply adaptive layouts. The adaptive skill uses NavigationSuiteScaffold + nav3 SceneStrategies for multi-pane.

findings.topic: adaptive skill: Grid API is experimental in Compose 1.11.0-beta01
findings.guidance: adaptive SKILL.md Step 4.2 warning: 'Grid is an experimental API available from Compose 1.11.0-beta01. Confirm with the user that they are happy to use an experimental API.' The current Compose BOM 2026.03.01 includes Compose 1.8.x; Grid at GA requires a future BOM update. For EditorScreen's option panel layout (sliders, color pickers arranged in a grid), use LazyVerticalGrid with GridCells.Adaptive() as the stable approach until Grid API graduates.

findings.topic: android CLI: skills install commands
findings.guidance: Install a specific skill into the current project directory: `android skills add --skill=<skill-name> --project=.`. Install all skills: `android skills add --all`. List available skills: `android skills list`. Find skills by keyword: `android skills find <keyword>`. Install the android CLI itself first (Mac ARM): `curl -fsSL https://dl.google.com/android/cli/latest/darwin_arm64/install.sh | bash`. Relevant individual install commands for EasyWatermark migration: `android skills add --skill=migrate-xml-views-to-jetpack-compose --project=.` and `android skills add --skill=navigation-3 --project=.` and `android skills add --skill=edge-to-edge --project=.` and `android skills add --skill=testing-setup --project=.` and `android skills add --skill=agp-9-upgrade --project=.` and `android skills add --skill=adaptive --project=.`.

findings.topic: android CLI: docs search for up-to-date API information

Recommended to use this during the migration for any API whose behavior is unclear, rather than relying on training data. Also `android docs fetch <url>` to retrieve specific documentation pages.
